_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Germany covering Germanic tribes (Arminius/Teutoburg Forest 9 CE), Frankish Empire/Charlemagne, Holy Roman Empire (962-1806, 'First Reich'), Hanseatic League, Reformation (Martin Luther 1517, Wittenberg), Thirty Years' War (1618-48, ~8M dead), Enlightenment (Kant, Goethe), Napoleonic Wars, Congress of Vienna, Revolutions 1848, Bismarck unification 1871 (Second Reich), Kaiser Wilhelm II, WWI (1914-18, 2M dead), Weimar Republic, Hitler/Nazi Germany (Third Reich 1933-45), WWII (1939-45, 7M German dead), Holocaust/Shoah (6M Jews murdered), division BRD/DDR (1949-90), Berlin Wall (1961-89), reunification 1990, EU engine, and economic powerhouse.

religion.note: Historic Protestant-Catholic divide (Reformation birthplace; north Protestant, south Catholic); declining rapidly (church exits accelerating ~500k/year); Muslim community (~5.5M, mostly Turkish); church tax (Kirchensteuer, 8-9% income tax surcharge, drives exits); East Germany most atheist region in world (DDR legacy)

ethnic_groups.name: German
ethnic_groups.notes: Germanic peoples; regional identities strong (Bavarian, Saxon, Swabian, etc.); reunification divided East/West identity; Vergangenheitsbewußtsein (coming to terms with past); Wirtschaftswunder (economic miracle)

ethnic_groups.name: Turkish/Kurdish
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest minority; Gastarbeiter (guest workers from 1960s, ~3M); integration debates; Döner kebab (Germany's most popular street food); political participation growing

ethnic_groups.name: Syrian
ethnic_groups.notes: 2015 refugee crisis (~1M arrived, Merkel's 'Wir schaffen das'); largest refugee intake in EU; integration challenge

ethnic_groups.name: Polish
ethnic_groups.notes: Historical community + EU migration; Silesian heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Other EU
ethnic_groups.notes: Italian, Romanian, Croatian, Greek, Spanish, Bulgarian; EU free movement

ethnic_groups.name: Other non-EU
ethnic_groups.notes: Ukrainian (2022 refugees ~1M), Afghan, Iraqi, Russian-German (Spätaussiedler ~4.5M post-1990 from former USSR); Sorbs (Slavic autochthonous, ~60k, Lusatia); Danish minority (Schleswig); Sinti and Roma

independence.from: Unification (Bismarck, Versailles Hall of Mirrors); modern: reunification 1990-10-03

country_profile.notes_unique: Martin Luther (95 Theses 1517, Wittenberg, Reformation that split Christianity); Holocaust/Shoah (6 million Jews murdered 1941-45, industrialised genocide, Auschwitz/Treblinka/Sobibór, unique moral catastrophe); Erinnerungskultur (remembrance culture, global model for confronting past); Berlin Wall (1961-89, Cold War symbol, fell November 9, 1989); reunification (October 3, 1990, peaceful, 'Wende', Ostalgie); EU engine (Franco-German axis, largest economy in Europe, 4th globally); Mittelstand (family-owned manufacturing companies, economic backbone); Autobahn (no speed limit sections); beer (Reinheitsgebot 1516, Oktoberfest, world's most diverse beer culture); Goethe/Schiller/Kant/Hegel/Marx/Nietzsche (intellectual tradition); Beethoven/Bach/Wagner/Brahms (musical tradition); engineering (Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Volkswagen, Siemens); Energiewende (energy transition, nuclear exit); Bundesliga (football); 52 UNESCO World Heritage Sites; Gutenberg (printing press ~1440)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Friedrich Merz
current_leader.title: Chancellor
current_leader.notes: CDU; conservative; lawyer; defeated Scholz's SPD February 2025 election; Merkel rival who finally won; coalition negotiations ongoing; pro-business; stricter immigration

head_of_state.name: Frank-Walter Steinmeier
head_of_state.title: Federal President
head_of_state.notes: SPD; former Foreign Minister; ceremonial but moral authority; re-elected 2022; Ukraine crisis speeches; consensus figure

former_leaders.name: Olaf Scholz
former_leaders.notes: SPD; 'traffic light' coalition (SPD/Greens/FDP); Zeitenwende ('turning point' speech, February 2022, €100B defence spending after Ukraine invasion); leadership questioned; FDP coalition collapsed November 2024; snap election February 2025; low approval

former_leaders.name: Angela Merkel
former_leaders.notes: CDU; first female chancellor; East German physicist; 16 years (4 terms, longest since Kohl); 'Mutti'; eurozone crisis manager; 2015 refugee decision ('Wir schaffen das', ~1M Syrian refugees); most powerful woman in world (Forbes, 14 times); retired voluntarily; Putin whisperer; steady, cautious; defined an era

former_leaders.name: Gerhard Schröder
former_leaders.notes: SPD; Agenda 2010 reforms (labour market liberalisation, controversial); opposed Iraq War 2003; Gazprom/Putin friendship (widely condemned post-2022); Hartz IV welfare reform

former_leaders.name: Helmut Kohl
former_leaders.notes: CDU; 'Chancellor of Unity'; reunification architect (negotiated with Gorbachev/Bush/Mitterrand/Thatcher, October 1990); Maastricht Treaty/Euro; longest-serving post-war (16 years); financial scandal (slush funds); died 2017; 'greatest chancellor since Adenauer'

former_leaders.name: Helmut Schmidt
former_leaders.notes: SPD; crisis manager (terrorism, RAF/Baader-Meinhof, Mogadishu hijacking); economics; NATO Double-Track Decision; died 2015; respected elder statesman

former_leaders.name: Willy Brandt
former_leaders.notes: SPD; Ostpolitik (Eastern policy, rapprochement with East Germany/Poland/USSR); Warsaw genuflection 1970 (Kniefall, knelt at Warsaw Ghetto memorial, iconic); Nobel Peace Prize 1971; Berlin mayor; resigned (Guillaume spy affair); moral authority

former_leaders.name: Konrad Adenauer
former_leaders.notes: CDU; first chancellor of West Germany (BRD); Wirtschaftswunder architect (with Erhard); Western integration (NATO, EU founding, Franco-German reconciliation); 'Der Alte' (The Old Man, served until 87); Rhineland Catholic; defined postwar Germany
